summary: Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, and Hidenaka Tanaka. He taught at Kyoto University (~1946–1949) and held professorships at Tokai University (~1967–1973), Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana University, and Soka University.

Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He was affiliated with the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947), the University of Pennsylvania (1951–1954), and under Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi (b. 1928) specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1967–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida (b. 1954) specializes in linguistics, Japanology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018, professor from 1996, emeritus 2018) and Kyoto University (~2006–2020).

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He served as an associate professor at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) worked in sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady, later holding a post at Peking University (~1923–1926).

Yuto Kawamura is an Indologist who held a postdoctoral fellowship at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and academic posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) specialized in sinology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University (1978), the University of Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Yönten Gyatso (1932–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned degrees at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies at EPHE (~1980–1997).
Yūki Takamu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Takamu pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served as a part-time lecturer there (attested 2017).
Zack Beer is a Buddhist studies scholar who has studied at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2026) and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Zaifu Liu (1941–2026) worked in sinology. After studying at Xiamen University (~1959–1963), he directed the Institute of Literature at CASS (1985–1989) and taught at Chicago (~1989–1990), Stockholm (~1991–1992), Colorado Boulder (~1992), CityU Hong Kong (2004), and HKUST.

Zarawar Khan specializes in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned MA and PhD degrees in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929) under Pe Maung Tin and later pursued studies at the University of Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zeff Bjerken works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and several traditional teachers, and held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).
Zellig S. Harris (1909–1992) was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University.

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1931 to 1934 under Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of California (~1944–1947) and under teachers Jōshin Kasai, Richard Baker, and Sojun Mel Weitsman, later serving as co-abbess of the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
